source.note: Table 5 transcribed directly. Cumulative-depth arithmetic checked and reconciles cleanly for all 4 finite layers (unlike Bori/Etche, no inconsistency found here).
source.curve_type_note: Paper's own text (Discussion) states the trend as ℓ1<ℓ2>ℓ3<ℓ4<ℓ5 - NOT monotonic (real dip at layer 3) - yet the paper still calls it an 'A-type curve' throughout. This is the THIRD confirmed instance (after Etche's Odufor and Opiro) of this research community using 'A-type' as a loose descriptor for 'broadly increasing with depth' rather than the strict monotonic definition. Our classifier correctly declines to assert a specific type here (5 layers, non-monotonic -> 'unclassified' per interpret_layers.py's calibrated rule) rather than parroting the paper's looser label.

stations.curve_type_published: A (loosely - see curve_type_note, real sequence is not monotonic)
